finalText:
Green: 625/625 passing, exit 0.

**What was actually broken** — a single bug in `src/pricing.js:39` `orderTotal`. Only 3 of the 625 cases failed, all in the "order totals" suite; everything else was noise.

The function discounted the order correctly but then computed tax on the **pre-discount** amount:

```js
const tax = roundCents(cents * taxRate);   // `cents`, not `discounted`
return discounted + tax;
```

That contradicted its own doc comment ("tax is charged on the amount the customer pays"), so customers were overcharged tax on the discounted-away portion — the overcharge scaled with discount × rate (e.g. +668 cents on the 33400c / 10% off / 20% tax case).

Fix: tax the discounted subtotal, reusing the existing helper.

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
return applyTax(discounted, taxRate);
```

One note: this rounds twice (once after the discount, once after tax), which is what the other functions do and what all three expected values assume — e.g. 12000 → 10200 → 11041.5 → 11042. If your ledger actually wants a single rounding at the end, that's a different (and slightly different-valued) change, so I left the existing convention alone.
